rules.title: GraphQL introspection enabled in production config
rules.description: Introspection publishes the full schema, including fields and mutations that are not referenced by any client. It is not a vulnerability on its own, but it turns an unauthenticated endpoint into a map of one.
rules.remediation: Disable introspection outside development, and rely on authorization rather than obscurity for the fields that matter.

rules.title: GraphQL server without a depth or complexity limit
rules.description: A recursive query against a cyclic schema expands exponentially. Without a depth or cost limit a single request can exhaust the server.
rules.remediation: Add graphql-depth-limit or a cost analysis rule to validationRules.

rules.title: Request body spread into a model update
rules.description: Spreading the body lets a client set any field on the document, including role, balance or ownership.
rules.remediation: Pick the fields explicitly, or validate against a schema that strips unknown keys.

rules.title: Authentication endpoint with no rate limiting nearby
rules.description: Without throttling, credential stuffing and OTP brute force are limited only by network bandwidth.
rules.remediation: Apply a rate limiter keyed on the account and on the source address, and back off exponentially on failures.

rules.title: Exception detail returned to the client
rules.description: Stack traces and exception text leak file paths, library versions, SQL fragments and sometimes credentials from connection strings.
rules.remediation: Log the detail server-side with a correlation id, return the id and a generic message.

rules.title: JWT issued with a very long or absent expiry
rules.description: A token that lives for months cannot be revoked by expiry, so a leaked one stays useful for months.
rules.remediation: Keep access tokens short (minutes) and use a refresh token you can revoke server-side.

rules.title: WebSocket server without an origin check
rules.description: WebSocket handshakes are not covered by the same-origin policy. Without an origin check, any page can open an authenticated socket using the visitor's cookies - cross-site WebSocket hijacking.
rules.remediation: Validate the Origin header against an allowlist in verifyClient, and authenticate with a token rather than a cookie.

rules.title: Android component exported without a permission
rules.description: An exported component with no permission can be started by any other app on the device.
rules.remediation: Set exported="false", or require a signature-level permission.

rules.title: Cleartext HTTP traffic permitted
rules.description: Allowing cleartext means any network the device joins can read and rewrite the app's traffic.
rules.remediation: Remove the flag and fix the endpoints that still need HTTP.
